results.corrected_title: IBM shares fall about 7% after earnings beat as Krishna says clients are scrutinising AI ROI
results.corrected_summary: On 21 October IBM reported Q3 2026 revenue of $17.1 billion (up 5%) and adjusted EPS of $2.95, both above estimates, but kept its full-year revenue growth outlook unchanged. On the earnings call CEO Arvind Krishna said large enterprises are becoming 'a lot more cognizant' of the true ROI of their AI spend and are 'getting worried if some of the AI spending [is] completely out of control with no real return.' The shares fell about 7% to $233.50 in morning trading on 22 October. Accenture fell 0.5% and Infosys fell 2%.
key_facts: Q3 2026 results released 21 October 2026: revenue $17.1bn vs about $16.82bn expected; adjusted EPS $2.95 vs about $2.86-2.87 consensus
Full-year guidance kept at 4-5% constant-currency revenue growth; software revenue was $7.8bn, up 8%
Krishna's quote was about client worries, given during analyst Q&A, not a warning he issued himself
IBM fell about 7% to $233.50 on the morning of 22 October, after rising 3.96% to $251.49 on 21 October and slipping after hours
Accenture fell 0.5% to $239; Infosys fell 2% to $12.44
results.issues: The candidate frames Krishna as warning that AI spending is out of control. In the transcript he is describing what enterprise clients worry about. 24/7 Wall St. links the drop partly to the unchanged full-year forecast. Consensus EPS is given as $2.86 in the transcript and $2.87 by 24/7 Wall St. The 7% intraday drop and $233.50 price come only from 24/7 Wall St.; I could not open CNBC (403).

results.corrected_title: UK announces about £600 million AI security package, including £100 million AI Biosecurity Lab
results.corrected_summary: Ahead of the Budget, the UK government announced roughly £600 million (about $800 million) for AI security. It includes £100 million for a new AI Biosecurity Lab, £65 million for countermeasures against dangerous pathogens, £120 million more for the AI Security Institute and £130 million for two cyber programmes (National Cyber Shield and the National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability Centre). OpenAI and Anthropic will commit up to £200 million in in-kind model credits and access to the biosecurity lab. OpenAI's share is £100 million and Anthropic's is up to £100 million.
key_facts: GOV.UK 'Introducing the AI Biosecurity Lab' published 24 October 2026: £100m government funding plus up to £200m in company commitments
OpenAI: £100m in compute and model credits plus trusted model access; Anthropic: up to £100m in model credits, model access and technical support
Wider package of about £600m: £65m for pathogen countermeasures, £120m for the AI Security Institute, £130m for cyber programmes
AI minister Kanishka Narayan commented; Google DeepMind and Basecamp Research will also provide support
Smaller items include £60m for robotics and manufacturing AI firms, £23m to study AI's economic impact, £18m for a chip design academy and £30m for regional mayors
results.issues: The GOV.UK page I opened covers only the biosecurity lab (£100m plus up to £200m). The £65m, £120m and £130m figures come from Reuters via Investing.com. The line items Reuters lists add up to about £621m, against the 'about £600m' headline. The company contributions are in-kind credits and access, not cash. One secondary source dates the briefing to 23 October, but the official release and Reuters are dated 24 October.

results.corrected_title: Amodei answers critics of Anthropic's leaked federal AI safety bill, calls its handling a mistake
results.corrected_summary: On 21 October Dario Amodei published a long post on X replying to critic Nathan Calvin of Encode, after backlash over a draft federal AI safety bill Anthropic had been circulating to lawmakers. Politico first reported the draft on 16 October. Under the draft, independent evaluators registered with Commerce could trigger a court request to halt a model's release if they found an imminent risk of more than 50 deaths or over $1 billion in damage. Safety advocates said the bar was too high and the preemption wording too weak. Amodei acknowledged mistakes and communication failures, including the leaked bill. Inside Defense reported he said the draft may have been a 'mistake', and Anthropic said it would rewrite parts of it.
key_facts: Politico first reported the draft on 16 October 2026; Anthropic confirmed it
Evaluators registered with Commerce would have 72 hours to report an imminent risk (over 50 deaths or over $1bn in damage); Commerce could then ask a D.C. federal judge to halt the release
Encode's Nathan Calvin and other safety advocates criticised the threshold and the preemption language
Amodei posted a long reply on X on 21 October, conceding mistakes and calling the leaked bill a communication failure
Anthropic said it would rewrite parts of the draft; no member of Congress has introduced it
results.issues: The bill itself is stale: Politico reported it on 16 October, before the window. Only Amodei's 21 October reply, and the backlash and rewrite pledge around it, falls inside the window, so the item is reframed around that. Inside Defense is paywalled and its excerpt does not give Amodei's exact 'mistake' wording. I did not open the original X post; its content comes from secondary reports. Cryptopolitan quotes Anthropic's Anthony Cimino calling the preemption wording 'not precise enough', but I could not confirm that quote elsewhere. I did not open the Washington Post link.
